topic: AWS AgentCore Memory with Claude Guide 2026: Context-Aware Enterprise Agents

competitors.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory: Building context-aware agents
key_points: Introduced at AWS Summit NYC 2025, AgentCore Memory solves the fundamental LLM statelessness problem
Two memory layers: short-term (raw events, session-scoped) and long-term (extracted insights, cross-session)
Three built-in memory strategies: Semantic (facts/knowledge), Summary (running conversation summaries), User Preferences (choices/styles)
Custom memory strategies allow overriding extraction prompts with domain-specific LLMs
Hierarchical namespaces for multi-tenant isolation: /org_id/user_id/preferences/ patterns
Branching enables alternative conversation paths from a root event (message editing, what-if scenarios)
Checkpointing saves agent state for multi-session task resumption
Event expiry configurable up to 365 days, encryption at rest and in transit
PII is automatically excluded from long-term memory extraction by default

competitors.title: What Is Amazon Bedrock AgentCore? The 2026 Guide for AWS Teams
key_points: AgentCore is a fully managed platform: write agent code, AgentCore handles infrastructure, session isolation, memory, tools, security, scaling, monitoring
Seven components: Runtime, Gateway, Memory, Identity, Observability, Built-in Tools (Browser + Code Interpreter), Policy and Evaluations
Runtime: serverless compute for agents, each session gets its own microVM, sessions up to 8 hours, 100MB payloads
Gateway: MCP-compatible tool access, wraps Lambda/APIs into agent-ready tools, handles OAuth and credential management
Identity: agent-level IAM, inbound auth via Okta/Entra/Cognito, outbound auth to Slack/GitHub/Zoom
Observability: step-by-step execution traces via CloudWatch + OpenTelemetry
Managed harness (April 2026): define agent with model + system prompt + tools, no orchestration code needed
AgentCore CLI with CDK support (April 2026), Terraform coming soon
Consumption-based pricing: $0.0895/vCPU-hour, idle time free, no upfront commitments
Typical production agent: $50-200/mo infrastructure + $200-800/mo inference for 10K conversations

competitors.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: How AWS Built an Enterprise Platform for AI Agent Deployment
key_points: Five tightly integrated services: Runtime, Gateway, Memory, Identity, Observability
Framework-agnostic: supports LangGraph, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, Strands Agents, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK
Runtime billing: $0.0895/vCPU-hour, billed per second, I/O wait and idle time free
Gateway: $0.005/1,000 tool invocations, MCP-compatible, handles OAuth ingress/egress
Memory: $0.25/1,000 short-term events, long-term memory persists across sessions
Competitive comparison: AgentCore is infrastructure platform vs Google ADK (framework-first) and OpenAI Agents SDK (lightweight framework)
Real-world adoption: Epsilon (30% faster campaigns, 8 hours saved/team/week), NVIDIA (NeMo integration guide)
A2A protocol support for multi-agent coordination across platforms
AWS lock-in on infrastructure layer but agent code is portable

competitors.title: Amazon launches AI Agents that stay within boundaries, track their performance, and get smarter over time
key_points: Policy in AgentCore: natural language rules enforced at Gateway layer via Cedar policies, blocks unauthorized actions in milliseconds
Example policy: 'Block all refunds when reimbursement amount is greater than $1,000'
AgentCore Evaluations: 13 pre-built evaluators (correctness, helpfulness, tool selection accuracy, safety, goal success rate, context relevance)
Continuous sampling of live agent interactions with proactive alerts for quality drift
Episodic memory: agents learn from past experiences, capture context/reasoning/actions/outcomes
Example: agent books airport transport 45min before for solo travel, 2 hours early for family trip based on past experience
Enterprise adopters: S&P Global (Astra platform), Druva, Natera, Cox Automotive, MongoDB, PGA TOUR, Thomson Reuters, Workday
S&P Global: agent deployment from weeks to minutes with AgentCore

competitors.title: AWS Bedrock for Enterprise Agents: Architecture & Context 2026
key_points: Bedrock Agents (older) is configuration-based managed experience; AgentCore is production platform for full control
AgentCore handles runtime, memory, tool access, authentication, and authorization as modular services
Together Bedrock + AgentCore give teams a complete platform without framework lock-in
Enterprise focus: session isolation, memory sanitization, identity-bound access, policy enforcement, audit logging
Compliance: HIPAA eligible, GDPR compliant, SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP authorized in GovCloud

AgentCore Memory costs $0.25 per 1,000 short-term memory events; long-term memory extraction is asynchronous and managed
AgentCore Gateway costs $0.005 per 1,000 tool invocations, with MCP-compatible protocol support
AgentCore supports sessions up to 8 hours long and 100MB payloads for multimodal workloads
Three built-in memory strategies: Semantic (facts/knowledge), Summary (conversation summaries), and User Preferences (choices/styles)
Custom memory strategies allow developers to choose a specific LLM and override extraction/consolidation prompts for domain-specific use cases
Event expiry in AgentCore Memory is configurable up to 365 days; data is encrypted at rest and in transit by default with optional customer-managed KMS keys
AgentCore Policy uses Cedar policy language enforced at the Gateway layer, blocking unauthorized actions in milliseconds
AgentCore Evaluations provides 13 pre-built evaluators for correctness, helpfulness, tool selection accuracy, safety, goal success rate, and context relevance

Typical production agent costs: $50-$200 per month in AgentCore infrastructure plus $200-$800 in Bedrock model inference for 10,000 conversations/month
